title: Backup Job Success and Freshness
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric event=backup
| stats latest(status) as last_status, max(_time) as last_backup by vm_name
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_backup)/3600,1)
| where last_status!="ok" OR hours_since>36
| sort - hours_since
description: Confirms that every virtual machine and dataset actually backed up recently and successfully, closing the gap between assuming and knowing.
value: The worst time to discover a broken backup is during a restore; freshness and success checks make your safety net trustworthy.
implementation: Forward backup job results; schedule daily and alert on any failed or overdue backup.
visualization: Table of protected items by last backup status and age.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Proxmox VE — Universal Forwarder + collectd/telegraf or API poll → HEC.
• **Subcategory context**: Home Lab & Self-Hosting — typical feeds: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `proxmox:metric`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Proxmox VE** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=proxmox:metric`.

**Collection method:** Universal Forwarder + collectd/telegraf or API poll → HEC.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `GET /api2/json/nodes/{node}/qemu`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 300s.

**Key fields to extract:** `vmid, name, cpu, mem, disk, status`.

**Typical connector stack:** Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC..

**Author notes:** Forward backup job results; schedule daily and alert on any failed or overdue backup.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "proxmox:metric", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Backup Job Success and Freshness** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=proxmox:metric`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `hours_since` (> 36) after latest, max — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `hours_since`, `vm_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric event=backup
| stats latest(status) as last_status, max(_time) as last_backup by vm_name
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_backup)/3600,1)
| where last_status!="ok" OR hours_since>36
| sort - hours_since
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Proxmox web UI → node summary. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table hours_since, vm_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `hours_since` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(hours_since) AS p50 perc90(hours_since) AS p90 perc99(hours_since) AS p99 max(hours_since) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.8.6: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Protected Items By Last Backup Status And Age (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Proxmox VE — no Proxmox VE events / missing fields:** If `proxmox:metric` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Proxmox VE connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Proxmox VE — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Proxmox VE JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Proxmox VE — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Proxmox VE — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Proxmox VE APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
